blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: Cross-Training for Your Brain
blocks.content: Just like a gym workout targets different muscle groups, the Math Gym targets different mathematical skills. It bundles together 7 different mini-games covering decimals, functions, dot products, fractions, linear equations, indices, and polynomials. The gym adapts to your level, making problems harder when you're succeeding and easier when you're struggling.

blocks.title: 2. The Strategy: Warm Up Then Push Hard
blocks.content:
Like any workout:

• Start with topics you're comfortable with (warm-up).
• Gradually move to harder challenges.
• Don't skip topics you find difficult! That's where the growth happens.
• Track your accuracy rates. Aim for 80%+ on each topic before moving on.

blocks.title: 3. The Method: Rotation System
blocks.content:
The Gym cycles through different exercise types:

1. **Decimals:** Signed decimal multiplication.
2. **Functions:** Polynomial evaluation.
3. **Dot Products:** 2D and 3D vector products.
4. **Fractions:** Adding fractions with different denominators.
5. **Linear Equations:** Solving for x.
6. **Indices:** Applying index laws.
7. **Polynomials:** Monomial algebra.

blocks.title: 4. Pro Tip: Use It as Exam Prep
blocks.content:
The Gym is the perfect exam preparation tool because it:

• Forces context switching between topics (just like a real exam).
• Keeps you sharp on fundamentals.
• Identifies weak areas automatically.
• Builds speed and confidence under pressure.

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: Don't treat the Gym as a one-time activity! Mathematical fitness, like physical fitness, requires regular practice. Doing the gym once won't help. Aim for 15-20 minutes per day, 3-4 days per week. Consistency beats intensity. Also, don't just rush through problems. Quality matters more than quantity.
